name: fix_shell_backup_script_hardening
description: Harden a fragile bash backup script: strict mode, quoted expansions, glob instead of $(ls), argument validation - proven against paths with spaces
prompts: scripts/backup.sh copies every .conf file from a source directory into a destination directory, writes an `ls`-style manifest.txt inside the destination, and prints 'backup complete'. It is fragile the classic ways: no strict mode (a failed copy still reports success and exits 0), every expansion is unquoted (any path containing a space shatters into separate words), it iterates over $(ls ...) output instead of a glob, and it doesn't check its arguments. Harden it: enable `set -euo pipefail`; validate that exactly two arguments were given (usage message to stderr and non-zero exit otherwise); quote every expansion; iterate the .conf files with a shell glob (mind the no-matches case - e.g. nullglob) rather than parsing ls. The observable behavior for well-formed runs is unchanged: same files copied, same manifest, same success message - and it must now work when SRC, DEST, or the .conf filenames contain spaces.

setup_files.scripts/backup.sh:
#!/bin/bash
# Nightly backup: copy every .conf file from SRC into DEST, then write a
# manifest of DEST's contents and report success.
SRC=$1
DEST=$2

mkdir -p $DEST
for f in $(ls $SRC/*.conf); do
  cp $f $DEST
done
ls $DEST > $DEST/manifest.txt
echo "backup complete"

test_setup_files.check_backup.py:
"""Behavioral checks for scripts/backup.sh, run with the real bash."""
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT = "scripts/backup.sh"


def run(*args):
    # Relative POSIX-style paths: identical meaning to bash on Linux and on
    # a Windows host's git-bash (absolute C:\ paths would be mangled there).
    return subprocess.run(
        ["bash", SCRIPT, *[str(a).replace("\\", "/") for a in args]],
        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30,
    )


# 1. Paths with spaces - the classic unquoted-expansion killer.
base = Path("backup_check_tmp")
shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True)
src = base / "my configs"
dest = base / "out dir"
src.mkdir(parents=True)
(src / "app one.conf").write_text("a=1\n", encoding="utf-8")
(src / "app two.conf").write_text("b=2\n", encoding="utf-8")
(src / "notes.txt").write_text("not a conf\n", encoding="utf-8")

proc = run(str(src), str(dest))
assert proc.returncode == 0, (
    f"backup of paths containing spaces failed (exit {proc.returncode}):\n"
    f"{proc.stdout}{proc.stderr}")
assert "backup complete" in proc.stdout, "success message lost"

copied = sorted(p.name for p in dest.glob("*.conf"))
assert copied == ["app one.conf", "app two.conf"], (
    f"expected both .conf files (and only those) in DEST, got {copied}; "
    f"unquoted expansions split names on spaces")
assert (dest / "app one.conf").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "a=1\n"

manifest = (dest / "manifest.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
assert "app one.conf" in manifest and "app two.conf" in manifest, (
    f"manifest incomplete:\n{manifest}")

# 2. Stray split-off fragments must not exist anywhere in DEST's parent.
stray = [p.name for p in base.rglob("*")
         if p.is_file() and p.name in ("app", "one.conf", "two.conf")]
assert not stray, f"word-splitting scattered fragments: {stray}"

# 3. Missing arguments must fail loudly, not plough on.
proc = run()
assert proc.returncode != 0, "running with no arguments must exit non-zero"

proc = run(str(src))
assert proc.returncode != 0, "running with one argument must exit non-zero"

print("PASS backup.sh hardening checks")

reference_solution.scripts/backup.sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Nightly backup: copy every .conf file from SRC into DEST, then write a
# manifest of DEST's contents and report success.
if [[ $# -ne 2 ]]; then
  echo "usage: backup.sh SRC DEST" >&2
  exit 1
fi

SRC=$1
DEST=$2

mkdir -p "$DEST"
shopt -s nullglob
for f in "$SRC"/*.conf; do
  cp "$f" "$DEST"
done
ls "$DEST" > "$DEST/manifest.txt"
echo "backup complete"
